selection: Twentieth-century Nigerian mythic fantasy rooted in Yoruba oral tradition, shifting the rotation from Miguel de Cervantes’s early-modern Spanish satire and extending the collection’s representation of African speculative fiction.

sources.use: Publisher biography for Tutuola’s 1920–1997 lifespan, the 1952 publication of his first novel, and the 1990 publication of his last book.

verifiedScope.dateDistinctions: Markers use first English-language book-publication years, not composition, later national editions, reissues or translations. The Palm-Wine Drinkard first appeared through Faber in Britain in 1952 and through Grove in the United States in 1953. The Wild Hunter in the Bush of the Ghosts was written earlier but first published in 1982, so it does not precede the publication bar. Later story and folktale books, including the 1990 Village Witch Doctor and Other Stories, are outside this novel-only scope.
verifiedScope.chartRange: Tutuola’s 1920–1997 lifespan already falls within the collection-derived chart domain, so no chart-range change was required.
